newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian long bonds surge on offshore interest.
newsitem.headline: Australian long bonds surge on offshore interest.

text.p: *Australian bonds find solid demand from offshore, aided by local expectations of lower rates, to shrug off weaker Treasuries and rally strongly on day of RBA board meeting.
*10-year futures post highest close since mid-June

Australian bonds put in a solid performance, led by the long end, as the market found favour with offshore investors and remained underpinned by expectations a rate cut will follow Tuesday's Reserve Bank board meeting.

The buying was spread through the day, with a late surge taking the September 10-year futures contract to its highest close since it became active in mid-June, with the yield on the benchmark bond ending back below 7.0 percent.
"It was a pretty solid performance all day," one trader said, saying the market was underpinned by rate cut expectations and buying thought to be associated with an upcoming debt issue.
"There was offshore buying last night which gave us a good bid tone early, then this afternoon obviously someone's pricing some sort of deal or issue," he said.
There was also offshore hedge fund buying of futures through the afternoon which traders said took the market to its highs.
The buying happened on the day of an RBA board meeting that is widely expected to sanction another cut in official interest rates, which are currently at 5.50 percent.
Short securities are expected to be well-supported ahead of the 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) announcement time for a rate cut, although markets do not expect any change on Wednesday.

Instead a move is favoured on Thursday, after the outcome of the U.S. FOMC is known, or after the release of wages and inflation data is known later this month. There is also a view that the RBA will hold off a cut until after its August meeting.
Apart from a possible rate cut, markets will also be watching the release of retail trade and building approvals data for May on Wednesday.
Retail trade is forecast to rise by 2.0 percent after falling 1.7 percent, while building approvals are expected to also rise 2.0 percent, continuing the housing sector's modest upturn.

Spreads narrow across the board, most notably against Canada, and long end strength sees curve flatten. Outperformance against Canada reflects some of the offshore buying of bonds and Australian dollars against Canadian dollar seen overnight and on Tuesday.
